title: 6 Areas You Can Help Your Pastor in Your Church
paragraphs: 6 Areas You Can Help Your Pastor in Your Church
There are battles your pastor fights that most people will never see.
Not because he hides them well.
But because shepherds often bleed silently.
People see the sermon. They hear the prayer. They notice the handshake. They admire the wisdom.
But they do not always see the burden.

They do not see the late-night calls when someone is dying. The private tears after counseling broken marriages. The spiritual warfare after preaching truth. The exhaustion of carrying families in prayer while his own soul quietly gasps for strength.
And maybe the saddest part of all...
Some pastors stand every Sunday surrounded by crowds... while secretly feeling completely alone.
The Apostle Paul understood this kind of burden deeply.
In 2 Corinthians 11:28, Paul wrote:
“Besides the other things, what comes upon me daily: my deep concern for all the churches.”
The Greek phrase for “deep concern” is:
ἡ μέριμνα (hē merimna)
It means anxiety, pressure, weight, inward burden.
Paul was not speaking about casual ministry stress.
He was describing the crushing spiritual responsibility of caring for souls.
This is why churches must stop treating pastors like spiritual machines.
Your pastor is not just a preacher. He is a man carrying eternal responsibility before God.
Hebrews 13:17 says:
“They watch out for your souls, as those who must give account.”
The Greek phrase for “watch out” is:
ἀγρυπνοῦσιν (agrypnousin)
It literally means:
“To stay awake.” “To lose sleep.” “To remain spiritually alert.”
Imagine that.
The calling of a true pastor is so heavy that Scripture describes it as losing sleep over souls.
And yet many believers only approach pastors when they need something.
Few ask:
“How can I strengthen the shepherd who strengthens us?”
This generation desperately needs to rediscover biblical partnership inside the church.
Not celebrity Christianity. Not consumer Christianity. Not entertainment-driven church culture.
But covenant. Burden-sharing. Kingdom responsibility. Biblical love.
Because healthy churches are not built by one exhausted pastor.
They are built by believers who understand that ministry belongs to the whole body of Christ.
Ephesians 4:11–12 says Christ gave pastors:
“For the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry.”
Notice that carefully.
The pastor equips. The saints minister.
The church was never supposed to function with one tired shepherd doing everything while everyone else spectates.
And maybe...
Maybe some pastors are burning out not because God failed them...
But because too many believers forgot their role in the Body.
If you have a faithful pastor who preaches biblical truth, guards doctrine, prays for souls, and points people to Jesus Christ...
You are more blessed than you realize.
So how can you help your pastor biblically?
Not through flattery. Not through empty compliments. Not through performative loyalty.
But in ways Scripture actually teaches.
The first area is prayer.
Most churches underestimate how violently spiritual ministry is opposed.
A pastor who faithfully preaches the Gospel becomes a target.
The enemy attacks marriages. Children. Mental health. Purity. Discouragement. Fatigue. Fear. Compromise.
This is why Paul repeatedly begged believers to pray for him.
In Ephesians 6:19, Paul wrote:
“And for me, that utterance may be given to me, that I may open my mouth boldly to make known the mystery of the gospel.”
The Greek word for boldly is:
παρρησία (parrēsia)
It means fearless confidence. Courageous speech. Unashamed proclamation.
Even Paul needed prayer for courage.
Think about that.
The man who survived prison, beatings, persecution, shipwrecks, and riots still asked believers to pray for boldness.
Your pastor does not just need applause after sermons.
He needs intercession before sermons.

Pray for his purity. Pray for his mind. Pray for his marriage. Pray for his children. Pray for protection from temptation. Pray against discouragement. Pray that he never compromises truth to gain approval.
There are sermons your pastor will only survive because somebody prayed.
The second area is encouragement.
Not fake hype. Not shallow compliments.
Real encouragement. Biblical encouragement.
Many pastors spend their lives pouring strength into others while receiving very little in return.
And words matter more than people realize.
Proverbs 12:25 says:
“Anxiety in the heart of man causes depression, but a good word makes it glad.”
The Hebrew phrase for “good word” comes from:
דָּבָר טוֹב (dāḇār ṭôḇ)
It means a beneficial word. A healing word. A restorative word.
Never underestimate what one sincere message can do.
“Pastor, that sermon helped save my marriage.” “Pastor, thank you for preaching truth even when it’s hard.” “Pastor, your prayers helped me survive this season.”
Sometimes one honest testimony gives a weary shepherd enough strength to keep going another month.
Do not only speak when you disagree. Speak when God uses him.
The third area is service.
Some churches exhaust pastors because nobody volunteers unless they receive attention.
But the Kingdom of God advances through servants.
Galatians 5:13 says:
“Through love serve one another.”
The Greek word for “serve” is:
δουλεύετε (douleuete)
It literally means:
“To become a servant.” “To willingly place yourself in service.”
Modern culture glorifies being noticed.
Jesus glorified washing feet.
There are pastors trying to preach, counsel, administrate, clean, organize, fix problems, disciple people, handle conflict, visit hospitals, and lead ministries simultaneously.
Not because they want control.
But because too few believers step forward.
Some of the holiest ministry in your church may never happen on a stage.
Holding a crying child in nursery. Cleaning after service. Helping elderly members. Welcoming visitors. Setting up chairs. Preparing meals. Driving someone to church. Answering messages.
Heaven notices hidden faithfulness.
Jesus said in Mark 10:45:
“For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.”
The King of Glory became a servant.
And somehow modern Christianity still struggles with humility.
The fourth area is protecting unity.
One of the greatest hidden pains pastors endure is church division.
Gossip destroys churches faster than persecution.
Satan does not always attack churches through atheists.
Sometimes he attacks through bitterness, offense, pride, jealousy, and careless words inside the congregation.
Proverbs 16:28 says:
“A whisperer separates close friends.”
The Hebrew idea behind whispering carries the image of secret slander. Quiet division. Poison spread slowly.
Some believers destroy spiritual families with their mouths while still singing worship songs on Sunday.
And pastors often stand in the middle trying to stop spiritual bleeding.
If you want to help your pastor...
Refuse gossip. Refuse division. Refuse unnecessary drama.
Romans 12:18 says:
“If it is possible, as much as depends on you, live peaceably with all men.”
Peace is not weakness.
Biblical unity is spiritual warfare.
A united church becomes dangerous to hell.
The fifth area is generosity.
This topic makes some people uncomfortable.
But Scripture speaks clearly.
A faithful church supports faithful ministry.
1 Timothy 5:17 says:
“Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and doctrine.”
The phrase “labor” comes from the Greek:
κοπιῶντες (kopiōntes)
It means exhausting toil. Working to the point of weariness.
Biblical ministry is labor.
Deep labor. Emotional labor. Spiritual labor. Mental labor.
And many pastors quietly carry financial stress while trying to care for others.
Generosity is not about worshiping money.
It is about removing unnecessary burdens so ministry can flourish.
Some believers spend more money monthly on entertainment than they ever invest into the Kingdom of God.
Yet the local church is where souls are discipled. Marriages restored. Children taught Scripture. Broken people introduced to Jesus Christ.
Healthy giving is not manipulation.
It is worship.
The sixth area is simply standing beside your pastor during difficult seasons.
Because one of the loneliest moments in ministry is discovering people only loved the pastor when life was easy.
When criticism rises... When attacks come... When misunderstandings spread... When exhaustion shows...
Some people disappear.
But faithful believers stay.
Aaron and Hur understood this principle long before the modern church existed.
In Exodus 17, while Israel fought Amalek, Moses became physically exhausted holding up his hands.
As long as his hands stayed raised, Israel prevailed.
When his strength failed, Aaron and Hur stood beside him and held his arms up.
The Hebrew imagery here is powerful.
This was not passive support.
This was covenant strengthening.
And many pastors today are spiritually standing on hills with trembling arms.
Not because they do not love God.
But because ministry is heavy.
Some pastors are smiling publicly while privately asking God for strength not to quit.
Imagine how many shepherds would survive if more believers became modern-day Aarons and Hurs.
Not worshiping pastors. Not idolizing leaders.
But strengthening faithful servants of God.
Because even shepherds need support.
And maybe while reading this...
You suddenly realized your pastor has been carrying far more than you knew.
Maybe God is exposing areas where you became spiritually passive.
Maybe you attended church faithfully while forgetting the people sacrificing to help feed your soul.
The early church understood shared responsibility.
Acts 2 describes believers carrying burdens together, serving together, praying together, giving together, suffering together.
Church was never designed to be a weekly religious performance.
It was family.
Real family.
And families carry one another.
Your pastor does not need perfection from you.
But faithful partnership can become oxygen to a weary shepherd.
One prayer. One encouraging message. One act of service. One defense against gossip. One generous act. One loyal stand during hardship.
These things matter more than you think.
Because pastors are human.
They feel disappointment. They battle exhaustion. They experience grief. They fight temptation. They endure criticism. They carry invisible burdens.
Yet every Sunday many still stand up and preach Jesus Christ anyway.
That kind of faithfulness should never be taken lightly.
And if God has blessed your church with a pastor who truly preaches biblical truth... Protect that gift. Pray for that gift. Strengthen that gift.
Because biblically faithful shepherds are becoming increasingly rare in this generation.
1 Thessalonians 5:12–13 says:
“Recognize those who labor among you, and are over you in the Lord and admonish you, and esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake.”
This does not mean pastors are above correction.
It means faithful spiritual leadership should not be treated casually.
One day many believers may realize too late how deeply their pastors fought to protect them spiritually.
And maybe tonight...
Somebody reading this suddenly feels convicted.
Not condemned.
Convicted.
Because the Holy Spirit is reminding you that church is not a place you consume.
It is a Body you help strengthen.
Some pastors silently read these testimonies and find strength to keep going.
Save this so you never forget the responsibility believers have toward those who watch over souls.
One exhausted shepherd strengthened by faithful believers can impact generations for the Kingdom of God.
Filipino Version:
6 Na Paraan Kung Paano Mo Matutulungan ang Iyong Pastor sa Simbahan
May mga laban ang pastor mo na malamang hindi mo kailanman makikita.
Hindi dahil magaling siyang magtago.
Kundi dahil maraming pastol ang tahimik na dumudugo.
Nakikita ng mga tao ang sermon. Naririnig nila ang panalangin. Napapansin nila ang ngiti. Humahanga sila sa karunungan.
Pero hindi nila nakikita ang bigat.

Hindi nila nakikita ang mga gabing walang tulog dahil may miyembrong gustong sumuko sa buhay. Hindi nila nakikita ang tahimik na pag-iyak matapos mag-counsel ng wasak na pamilya. Hindi nila nakikita ang spiritual warfare matapos mangaral ng katotohanan. Hindi nila nakikita ang pagod ng isang lalaking pasan ang mga kaluluwa habang unti-unti namang nauubos ang sarili niyang lakas.
At minsan...
Ang pinakamasakit na parte...
May mga pastor na napapalibutan ng maraming tao tuwing Linggo... pero pakiramdam nila mag-isa sila.
Naunawaan ito ni Apostol Pablo.
Sa 2 Corinthians 11:28 sinabi niya:
“Bukod pa sa ibang mga bagay, araw-araw ay nasa akin ang pagmamalasakit sa lahat ng mga iglesia.”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “pagmamalasakit” ay:
ἡ μέριμνα (hē merimna)
Ibig sabihin nito:
matinding bigat, pressure, inner burden, malalim na pag-aalala.
Hindi simpleng stress lang ang tinutukoy ni Pablo.
Ang tinutukoy niya ay ang mabigat na responsibilidad ng pag-aalaga ng mga kaluluwa.
Kaya maling isipin na ang pastor ay parang makina lang na hindi napapagod.
Ang pastor ay hindi lang preacher.
Isa siyang taong may pananagutang espiritwal sa harap ng Diyos.
Sinasabi sa Hebrews 13:17:
“Sila’y nagpupuyat dahil sa inyong mga kaluluwa.”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “nagpupuyat” ay:
ἀγρυπνοῦσιν (agrypnousin)
Literal itong nangangahulugang:
“manatiling gising,” “mawalan ng tulog,” “maging alerto espiritwal.”
Napakalalim niyan.
Ibig sabihin may mga pastor na nawawalan ng tulog dahil iniisip nila ang kalagayan ng mga tao sa simbahan.
Pero nakakalungkot...
Maraming believers ang lalapit lang sa pastor kapag may kailangan sila.
Kaunti lang ang nagtatanong:
“Pastor, paano po namin kayo matutulungan?”
Kailangan muling matutunan ng simbahan ang tunay na biblical partnership.
Hindi celebrity Christianity. Hindi consumer Christianity. Hindi entertainment church.
Kundi burden-sharing. Pagdadamayan. Pagmamahalan. Pananagutang espiritwal.
Dahil ang healthy na simbahan ay hindi itinayo ng isang pagod na pastor.
Itinayo ito ng mga mananampalatayang nauunawaan na ang ministry ay responsibilidad ng buong katawan ni Cristo.
Sa Ephesians 4:11–12:
“Upang ihanda ang mga banal sa gawain ng paglilingkod.”
Napakahalaga niyan.
Ang pastor ang naghahanda. Ang mga mananampalataya ang gumagawa ng ministry.
Hindi kailanman plano ng Diyos na isang tao lang ang bubuhat ng lahat habang ang iba ay nanonood lang.
At baka...
Baka may mga pastor ngayon na gusto nang sumuko hindi dahil iniwan sila ng Diyos...
Kundi dahil masyadong maraming believers ang nakalimot sa kanilang responsibilidad.
Kung may pastor ka na tapat na nangangaral ng Biblia... na pinoprotektahan ang katotohanan... na nananalangin para sa mga tao... na dinadala ang mga kaluluwa kay Jesus...
Mas pinagpala ka kaysa sa naiisip mo.
Kaya paano mo siya matutulungan?
Hindi sa puro papuri lang. Hindi sa fake loyalty. Hindi sa pagpapakitang-tao.
Kundi sa mga paraang itinuturo mismo ng Kasulatan.
Ang unang paraan ay panalangin.
Masyadong minamaliit ng maraming tao ang spiritual warfare laban sa mga pastor.
Kapag tapat na ipinapangaral ng isang pastor ang Ebanghelyo, nagiging target siya.
Ina-atake ang kanyang isip. Ang kanyang asawa. Ang kanyang mga anak. Ang kanyang purity. Ang kanyang emotional strength.
Kaya paulit-ulit humihingi si Pablo ng panalangin.
Sa Ephesians 6:19:
“Ipanalangin ninyo na ako’y pagkalooban ng pananalitang may katapangan.”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “katapangan” ay:
παρρησία (parrēsia)
Ibig sabihin:
fearless confidence, walang takot na pangangaral, matapang na pagsasalita ng katotohanan.
Isipin mo iyon.
Kahit si Pablo nangailangan ng panalangin.
Hindi kailangan ng pastor mo ng palakpak lang pagkatapos ng sermon.
Kailangan niya ng mga taong mananalangin bago pa siya tumayo sa pulpito.
Ipanalangin mo ang kanyang isip. Ang kanyang pamilya. Ang kanyang holiness. Ang kanyang courage. Ang kanyang spiritual protection.
May mga sermon na nasusurvive lang ng pastor dahil may mga taong nananalangin.
Ang pangalawang paraan ay encouragement.
Hindi fake compliments. Hindi plastic.
Tunay na encouragement.
Maraming pastor ang buong buhay nagbibigay lakas sa iba habang tahimik namang nauubos.
At minsan isang mensahe lang ang kailangan nila para hindi sumuko.
Sinasabi sa Proverbs 12:25:
“Ang mabuting salita ay nagpapasaya ng puso.”
Ang Hebrew phrase dito ay:
דָּבָר טוֹב (dāḇār ṭôḇ)
Ibig sabihin:
healing word, restorative word, beneficial word.
Huwag mong maliitin ang simpleng:
“Pastor, salamat po sa sermon.” “Pastor, nakatulong po iyon sa pamilya namin.” “Pastor, salamat po dahil hindi ninyo kinokompromiso ang katotohanan.”
Minsan sapat na iyon para lumaban ulit ang isang pagod na pastor.
Ang pangatlong paraan ay paglilingkod.
May mga simbahan na sobrang napapagod ang pastor dahil walang gustong tumulong maliban kung mapapansin sila.
Pero ang Kaharian ng Diyos ay itinatayo ng mga lingkod.
Galatians 5:13:
“Sa pamamagitan ng pag-ibig ay maglingkuran kayo.”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “maglingkuran” ay:
δουλεύετε (douleuete)
Literal na ibig sabihin:
“maging alipin sa paglilingkod,” “kusang maglingkod.”
Ang mundo gustong mapansin.
Si Jesus naghugas ng paa.
May mga pastor na nangangaral na nga... nagco-counsel pa... nag-aasikaso pa ng problema... nagvi-visit pa sa ospital... naglilinis pa... nag-aadjust pa ng sound system...
Hindi dahil gusto nila kontrolin lahat.
Kundi dahil kakaunti ang gustong tumulong.
Hindi lahat ng ministry nasa stage.
Minsan ang pinaka-holy na ministry ay:
pag-aalaga ng bata, pag-aayos ng upuan, pag-welcome ng bisita, paglilinis, pagdadala ng pagkain, pagtulong sa matatanda.
Nakikita ng langit ang mga bagay na hindi pinapansin ng tao.
Ang pang-apat na paraan ay protektahan ang unity.
Isa sa pinakamasakit na dinadala ng maraming pastor ay church division.
Mas maraming simbahan ang sinisira ng tsismis kaysa persecution.
Hindi laging sa labas nanggagaling ang atake ni Satanas.
Minsan nanggagaling ito sa bitterness, selos, pride, offense, at walang kontrol na dila.
Sinasabi sa Proverbs 16:28:
“Ang mapanirang tao ay naghihiwalay ng magkakaibigan.”
Ang larawan sa Hebrew nito ay tahimik na lason.
Whispering. Secret division. Slow destruction.
May mga taong sumisira ng spiritual family gamit ang bibig nila habang umaawit pa rin tuwing Linggo.
Kung gusto mong tulungan ang pastor mo...
Tumanggi kang makisali sa gossip. Tumanggi kang maghasik ng division. Tumanggi kang magpalala ng drama.
Ang united na simbahan ay napakadelikado para sa impyerno.
Ang pang-limang paraan ay generosity.
Alam kong uncomfortable ito para sa iba.
Pero malinaw ang Biblia.
Ang tapat na ministry ay dapat suportahan.
Sa 1 Timothy 5:17:
“Ang mga matandang namumuno nang mabuti ay karapat-dapat sa dobleng karangalan.”
Ang salitang “nagpapagal” ay mula sa Greek na:
κοπιῶντες (kopiōntes)
Ibig sabihin:
working to exhaustion, pagpapagal hanggang mapagod.
Mabigat ang tunay na ministry.
Emotional labor. Spiritual labor. Mental labor.
At maraming pastor ang tahimik na may financial burden habang iniintindi ang problema ng iba.
Ang generosity ay hindi tungkol sa pagsamba sa pera.
Ito ay tungkol sa pagtulong upang mas maging malaya ang ministry.
Napakaraming tao ang kayang gumastos para sa luho pero halos walang investment sa Kaharian ng Diyos.
Samantalang ang simbahan ang lugar kung saan:
naliligtas ang mga kaluluwa, naibabalik ang pamilya, natuturuan ang mga anak, at nakikilala si Jesus.
Ang pang-anim na paraan ay manatili sa tabi ng pastor sa mahihirap na panahon.
Dahil isa sa pinakamalungkot na bahagi ng ministry ay kapag nalaman mong mahal ka lang ng tao kapag maayos ang lahat.
Kapag may criticism... Kapag may attacks... Kapag may misunderstanding... Kapag pagod na ang pastor...
May mga taong biglang nawawala.
Pero ang tunay na faithful believers nananatili.
Sa Exodus 17, habang nakikipaglaban ang Israel, napagod si Moises sa pagtataas ng kanyang kamay.
Habang nakataas ang kamay niya, nananalo ang Israel.
Pero nanghina siya.
Kaya lumapit sina Aaron at Hur at inalalayan ang kanyang mga braso.
Napakagandang larawan nito.
Hindi nila sinamba si Moises.
Tinulungan nila siya.
At maraming pastor ngayon ang parang si Moises.
Pagod. Nanginginig. Lumalaban.
Hindi dahil kulang ang pagmamahal nila sa Diyos.
Kundi dahil mabigat ang ministry.
May mga pastor na nakangiti sa harap ng congregation habang tahimik na humihingi ng lakas sa Diyos para hindi sumuko.
Isipin mo kung gaano karaming shepherds ang mananatiling matatag kung mas maraming believers ang magiging modern-day Aaron at Hur.
Hindi idolizing pastors.
Kundi strengthening faithful servants.
Dahil kahit ang shepherd minsan kailangang alalayan.
At baka habang binabasa mo ito...
Pinapakita ng Diyos na naging passive ka sa ministry.
Baka faithful kang umaattend ng church... pero nakalimutan mong may mga taong nagsasakripisyo para maalagaan ang kaluluwa mo.
Ang simbahan ay hindi weekly religious show.
Pamilya ito.
At ang tunay na pamilya nagtutulungan.
Hindi kailangan ng pastor mo ng perfection.
Pero ang simpleng:
isang panalangin, isang encouragement, isang act of service, isang pagtatanggol laban sa gossip, isang faithful presence,
ay kayang magbigay ng bagong lakas sa isang pagod na shepherd.
Dahil tao rin ang mga pastor.
Nasasaktan sila. Napapagod. Nadidiscourage. Natutukso. Umiiyak.
Pero tumatayo pa rin sila tuwing Linggo para ipangaral si Cristo.
At hindi dapat basta-basta iyon.
Kung pinagpala ka ng Diyos ng pastor na tapat sa Biblia...
Ipanalangin mo siya. Protektahan mo siya. Tulungan mo siya. Pahalagahan mo siya.
Dahil unti-unting nagiging bihira ang mga tapat na shepherds sa panahon ngayon.
At baka ngayong gabi...
May tinatamaan ang Diyos sa puso mo.
Hindi condemnation.
Conviction.
Dahil pinapaalala ng Holy Spirit na ang simbahan ay hindi lugar na kino-consume mo lang.
Ito ay Katawan na dapat mong tulungang palakasin.
Minsan ang simpleng testimonya sa comments nagbibigay lakas sa mga pastor na gusto nang sumuko.
Minsan isang pastor lang na pinalakas ng tapat na believers ang ginagamit ng Diyos para baguhin ang buong henerasyon.
